description: Continuation of use as a retail unit (Class E(a), including food sales), with external alterations to the front, rear and side elevations of the unit, demolition of the existing garden centre lean-to structure, provision of plant area, installation of new trolley bays in car park, cycle parking and other associated works. (Related to Planning Application ref. 50209/APP/2026/371)
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
REASON
To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans, numbers:
08901 Rev 02 - Site Location Plan
08902 Rev 05 - Proposed Site Plan
08905 Rev 03 - Proposed Ground Floor Area Plan
08905A Rev 03 - Proposed First Floor Area Plan
08904 Rev 03 - Proposed External Elevations
08202 Rev 01 - Proposed Roof Plan
and shall thereafter be retained/maintained for as long as the development remains in existence.
REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions of The London Plan (2021) and Hillingdon Local Plan Parts 1 (2012) and 2 (2020).
The development hereby permitted shall not be used/occupied until the following has been completed/carried out in accordance with the specified supporting plans and/or documents:
Design and Access Statement by Brookerflynn Architects
Planning and Retail Statement by Lichfields dated 12 February 2026
Response to Independent Retail Audit by Lichfields, ref. 70714/01/NG/JeH/41348494v1 dated 6 July 2026
Healthy Streets Transport Assessment by Caneparo Associates Ltd dated November 2025
Air Quality Assessment by RPS Group, ref. 794-ENV-EM-AIR-22727 Rev 1 dated 14/11/2025
An environmental noise impact assessment and survey report RevA by Sharps Acoustics dated 11 November 2025
Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Statement by RPS Group, ref. ENV-22687 dated November 2025
Water Cycle Strategy by Hoare Lea, ref. REP-0513243-XX-HLE-20251003 Rev 01 dated 03/10/2025
Energy and Sustainability Strategy by Hoare Lea, ref. 5600094-HL-XX-XX-RP-Y-402085-P03_01 dated 27 November 2025
Sustainability Stage

(i) the phasing of demolition and construction works;
(ii) the hours during which demolition and construction works shall take place;
(iii) construction vehicle routing to and from the site, including measures to minimise construction vehicle movements during peak periods;
(iv) arrangements for the loading and unloading of plant and materials;
(v) parking arrangements for contractors and site operatives;
(vi) measures to prevent mud, dirt and debris being deposited on the public highway, including wheel-washing facilities where necessary;
(vii) details of the storage of plant, demolition and construction materials on site;
(viii) measures to maintain safe pedestrian and cycle access around the site throughout the works;
(ix) measures to minimise dust and emissi

Prior to the installation of any external facing materials, details and samples of all external materials and finishes shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include, as appropriate:
- Cladding panels, including colour and finish
- Treatment/finish to existing brickwork
- Details of the junction between the proposed external treatment and the retained adjoining roof/elevation
- Entrance tiling
- Glazing and framing
- External doors
- Plant screening and fencing.
The development shall thereafter be carried out and retained in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and high-quality finish, having regard to the prominence of the proposed alterations and the concerns raised in relation to the detailed design treatment, in accordance with Policy DP3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Pl

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the flood-risk mitigation and resilience measures identified within the approved Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Statement by RPS Group (ref. ENV-22687 dated November 2025) and the Water Cycle Strategy by Hoare Lea (ref. REP-0513243-XX-HLE-20251003 Rev 01 dated 03/10/2025).
The identified measures shall be fully implemented before the relevant parts of the development are brought into use and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To ensure that the development remains safe for its lifetime and does not increase flood risk on or off the site, in accordance with Policies SI12 and SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMEI 9 and DMEI 10 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

The development shall be carried out and thereafter operated in accordance with the energy-efficiency and sustainability measures set out within the approved Energy and Sustainability Strategy by Hoare Lea (ref. 5600094-HL-XX-XX-RP-Y-402085-P03_01 dated 27 November 2025) and Sustainability Stage 2 Report - Part L 2021 by Hoare Lea (ref. 5600094-HLE-XX-XX-RP-ST-357000-M&S Part L compliance -Stage 2-P01 dated 17 November 2025).
The approved measures shall be implemented prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted and thereafter retained and maintained.
REASON

To minimise energy demand and carbon emissions and secure the sustainability benefits upon which the development has been assessed, in accordance with Policy SI2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMEI 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, the alterations to the car parking layout shown on the approved plans, including the provision of eight accessible parking spaces, seven parent-and-child spaces and the approved trolley bays, shall be completed and made available for use.
Those facilities shall thereafter be retained for their designated purposes.
REASON

To ensure satisfactory parking and inclusive-access arrangements and to safeguard the safe and efficient operation of the site, in accordance with Policies TR4 and TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, the 34 cycle parking spaces (17 no. Sheffield stands) shown on the approved plans shall be fully provided and made available for use.
The cycle parking shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To encourage sustainable modes of travel and ensure appropriate cycle parking provision, in accordance with Policies TR4 and TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies T2 and T5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
Prior to first occupation of the premises hereby permitted, a Staff Travel Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The Travel Plan shall include:
- Measures to encourage staff travel by walking, cycling, public transport and car sharing
- Details of the appointment and responsibilities of a Travel Plan Coordinator
- Modal-share targets
- Arrangements for implementation, monitoring and review
- Mechanisms for reporting the results of monitoring to the Local Planning Authority.
The approved Travel Plan shall thereafter be implemented, monitored and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To promote sustainable travel and reduce reliance on travel by private car, in accordance with Policies TR4 and TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
For the lifetime of the development hereby permitted, the rating level (LAr) of noise caused by its operation shall not exceed:
40 dB LAr,15min for any fifteen-minute period between 23:00 and 07:00; and
50 dB LAr,1hour for any one-hour period between 07:00 and 23:00,

determined at a position one metre free-field external to any window or door of any permanent residential or equivalently noise-sensitive premises, in accordance with 'Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound', British Standards Institution BS 4142:2014.
REASON

To ensure that occupants of nearby noise-sensitive premises would not be exposed to noise caused by the permitted development at a level likely to result in an adverse effect on health or quality of life, including when windows are fully open for ventilation and cooling, in accordance with Policy P3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (201
The retail premises shall not be open to customers outside the following hours:
08:00 to 22:00 Monday to Saturday; and
10:00 to 18:00 on Sundays and Bank/Public Holidays.
REASON

To safeguard the residential amenity of nearby occupiers, in accordance with Policy P3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
The total net retail sales floorspace within Unit 1, Victoria Retail Park, including any mezzanine floorspace, shall not exceed 4,131 square metres
REASON

The application has been assessed on the basis of the stated quantum of retail floorspace and any material increase could have different implications for the vitality and viability of nearby centres and the application of the sequential and retail impact tests, in accordance with Policies TC3 and TC4 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies SD6 and SD7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy E5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMTC 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
The net sales floorspace used as the food hall shall not exceed 1,686 square metres.
REASON

To ensure that the scale of food retailing remains within that assessed in the submitted Retail Impact Assessment and independent retail review, and to safeguard the vitality and viability of nearby centres, in accordance with Policies TC3 and TC4 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies SD6 and SD7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy E5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMTC 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

No more than 90% of the sales floorspace within the food hall may be used for the sale of convenience goods. For the avoidance of doubt, the remaining floorspace within the food hall may be used only for comparison goods sales.
REASON

To ensure that the quantum of convenience goods floorspace remains within that assessed in the submitted Retail Impact Assessment and independent retail review, and to safeguard the vitality and viability of nearby centres, in accordance with Policies TC3 and TC4 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies SD6 and SD7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy E5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMTC 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

No part of the mezzanine floorspace within the unit shall be used for the sale or display for sale of food or convenience goods. All food and convenience goods sales shall take place at ground-floor level only.
REASON

To ensure that the nature and distribution of retail floorspace remain consistent with the assumptions tested in the submitted retail evidence and to safeguard the vitality and viability of nearby centres, in accordance with Policies TC3 and TC4 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies SD6 and SD7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy E5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Policy DMTC 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to the first use of the premises following completion of the development hereby permitted, a Service and Delivery Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

-	measures to ensure that no more than one delivery or servicing vehicle attends the loading dock at any one time;
-	arrangements to ensure all servicing vehicles enter and leave the service yard in forward gear;

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), The London Plan (2021), and the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) and Supplementary Planning Guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably.

The Equality Act 2010 aims to safeguard individuals accessing goods, facilities, and services from discrimination based on a 'protected characteristic', including disability. In accordance with the Act, service providers must enhance access to and within their premises, especially when reasonable adjustments are feasible and straightforward to implement. The Act mandates that service providers proactively identify and eliminate barriers hindering disabled people.

The application site is located within a Critical Drainage Area. All developments in this area must contribute to managing the risk of flooding from surface water by reducing surface water runoff from the site. Therefore the applicant should minimise the water from the site entering the sewers. Water run off from any roof or hard paving associated with the development should be directed to a soakaway, or tank or made permeable.

There is a possibility that there may be some contaminating substances in the ground at the site. Our contaminated land record shows the site to be on a former contaminated land use. We would advise persons working on site to take basic precautions in relation to any contamination they may find. Therefore, the above advice is provided on the grounds of Health and Safety of the workers on site and to ensure the appropriate restoration of the site is done should there be any contamination identified during the development, where there is a need for ground work once such works are complete to minimise risk to the occupants of the site.

It is considered that a condition based on fixed noise levels is consistent with noise and planning policy by relating external noise levels to the point at which adverse effects on health and quality of life start to be observed. The limit values are intended to be consistent with the evidence base that is reflected in guidance: 'Guidance on Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings' BS8233 2014. This is combined with the assessment principles and procedures detailed in guidance: 'Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound' British Standards Institution BS4142 2014.' This is used to set reference time periods for the assessment and adjust measured or calculated LAeq values for character as detailed in BS4142 to determine the rating level.
